P1.zone_summary: People are accountable for outcomes without the authority to make the decisions those outcomes require, so they check before acting.
P1.constraint: People are accountable for outcomes without the authority to deliver them

forces.t: Decisions drift upward whenever things feel risky.
Control is added in response to problems, and each layer slows the next decision.
People who could decide don't believe they are allowed to, so they escalate to be safe.
The process for turning a decision into work doesn't carry it, so people carry it by hand.

P1.move: Clarify one decision right per team.
P1.blind: The organization may have normalised escalation as diligence.
P1.notDo: Don't fix this with an empowerment programme.
P1.question: Where are we holding people accountable for outcomes without giving them enough authority to achieve them?
P1.metric: Share of key decisions made without escalation

P2.zone_summary: The business keeps committing to more than the system has capacity to deliver, and nothing is formally stopped to make room.
P2.constraint: Too many priorities, and no clear sense of what to stop

forces.t: New priorities are added faster than old ones are retired.
The difficult conversation is being avoided, so the cause stays unnamed.
Commitments are made without anything being removed, so they compete for the same capacity.
Capacity is committed past what exists, and the shortfall lands on the least protected work.

P2.blind: Your organization may have normalised overload as a sign of ambition.
P2.question: What are we willing to stop doing to make room for what matters most?
P2.metric: Share of capacity on the top three priorities

P3.zone_summary: Your people appear capable and willing. The system around them doesn't carry the work, so they are compensating for it by hand.
P3.constraint: Performance depends on people working around the system

forces.t: Each recurrence is solved as a new event rather than traced to its cause.
Nothing about the current pattern requires anyone to act, so it persists.
The process for turning a decision into work doesn't carry it, so people carry it by hand.
Work stalls at handoffs between teams, where no one owns the whole.

P3.blind: Your team may have learned to work around the system rather than improve it.
P3.notDo: Don't fix this by hiring more of the people who make it happen.
P3.question: Where are exceptional people compensating for a system that should work without heroics?
P3.metric: Hours per week spent on recurring workarounds

P4.zone_summary: Leadership hasn't settled what matters most, so the organization is executing several answers at once and experiencing it as slowness.
P4.constraint: Leadership isn't aligned on what matters most

forces.t: The difficult conversation is being avoided, so the cause stays unnamed.
New priorities are added faster than old ones are retired.
Leadership disagreement is settled case by case instead of once, so it re-runs inside every decision.
Direction changes from the top before the last direction has been delivered, which teaches teams to wait.

P4.blind: Your leadership team may have learned to treat polite agreement as alignment.
P4.notDo: Don't fix this with a communication plan.
P4.question: If our leadership team's top-three lists differ, whose list is the organization actually executing?
P4.metric: Distinct "top priorities" named across the leadership team

P5.zone_summary: The system runs on filtered information, because raising a problem or disagreeing carries a cost. Everything else is downstream of that.
P5.constraint: It isn't safe to raise problems or disagree

forces.t: The difficult conversation is being avoided, so the cause stays unnamed.
Current incentives reward the behaviour that produces the friction.
People who could decide don't believe they are allowed to, so they escalate to be safe.
Commitments quietly lapse without consequence, so commitment has stopped meaning much.

P5.blind: The organization may have learned that silence is loyalty.
P5.notDo: Don't fix this with an anonymous survey or a values poster.
P5.question: What is the problem everyone knows about that hasn't been said in a leadership meeting?
P5.metric: Time between a problem being noticed and being raised with someone who can act

P6.zone_summary: People are working hard. Your best people are on the wrong problems, so the effort isn't landing where the business needs it.
P6.constraint: Your best people aren't on the highest-value problems

forces.t: Each recurrence is solved as a new event rather than traced to its cause.
Current incentives reward the behaviour that produces the friction.
Capacity is committed past what exists, and the shortfall lands on the least protected work.
Commitments are made without anything being removed, so they compete for the same capacity.

P6.move: Audit one week of your five best people.
P6.blind: Your organization may have normalised using its best people as the emergency service.
P6.notDo: Don't fix this by hiring more senior people.
P6.question: If our best people's calendars are the real strategy, what strategy are we executing?
P6.metric: Share of top talent time on the top three priorities

P7.zone_summary: Priorities aren't tied to what creates value, so the system executes hard against a scoreboard that doesn't decide anything.
P7.constraint: Priorities aren't clearly connected to how the business creates value

forces.t: Activity is measured and rewarded, so activity is what grows.
New priorities are added faster than old ones are retired.
Decisions wait on information that may never be enough, because the real gap is who is allowed to decide under uncertainty.
Commitments are made without anything being removed, so they compete for the same capacity.

P7.move: Trace each top priority to a value driver.
P7.blind: The organization may be optimising for functional performance while sacrificing overall business value.
P7.notDo: Don't fix this with more reporting.
P7.question: Which activities consume the most resources without creating proportional value?
P7.metric: Share of resources on priorities with a named value driver
